name: window.zoo
title: Extract/Replacing the Time Windows of Objects

origin.description: Extract the observations inside a time window.
origin.usage: window.zoo(x, index. = index(x), start = NULL, end = NULL, ...)

arguments.name: index.
arguments.text: Candidate indexes. Only observations whose index is in this set are eligible. The default is the series index.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: Lower bound, inclusive. NULL or NA leaves the bound open. A length-two numeric start is converted with the series frequency.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: Upper bound, inclusive. NULL or NA leaves the bound open. A length-two numeric end uses the same frequency conversion.

origin.details: Rows stay in the order of x. Membership in index. does not repeat a time that is listed twice. A length-two start or end is floor(year * frequency + period - 1 + 0.0001) / frequency when the series has a frequency and a numeric index.
origin.value: The window, as a zoo series.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(c(10, 20, 30, 40), 1:4)
z <- window(x, start = 2, end = 3)
show <- function(v) paste(vapply(as.numeric(v), function(a) if (is.na(a)) "NA" else sprintf("%.16g", a), ""), collapse = " ")
cat(show(coredata(z)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(show(index(z)), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Extract the observations inside a time window.

arguments.name: index_
arguments.text: Candidate indexes. Only observations whose index is in this set are eligible. The default is the series index.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: Lower bound, inclusive. None or NaN leaves the bound open. A length-two numeric start is converted with the series frequency.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: Upper bound, inclusive. None or NaN leaves the bound open. A length-two numeric end uses the same frequency conversion.

translation.details: Rows stay in the order of x. Membership does not repeat a time that is listed twice. A length-two start or end is floor(year * frequency + period - 1 + 0.0001) / frequency when the series has a frequency and a numeric index.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.window import window_zoo

def show(values):
    array = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    flat = array.reshape(-1, order="F") if array.ndim == 2 else array.reshape(-1)
    parts = []
    for value in flat:
        value = float(value)
        parts.append("NA" if math.isnan(value) else format(value, ".16g"))
    return " ".join(parts)

x = Zoo([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
z = window_zoo(x, start=2, end=3)
print(show(z.data))
print(show(z.index))
